source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Totowa campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity and 200,000 square feet of technical space, and nothing that says what density that power is built to serve.

The two figures are the whole published spec. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 6 MW is roughly 150 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 600. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so the building's actual rack count is unknown and the conversion is an outside estimate, not a disclosed fact.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which concerns controls over financial reporting, not power or cooling. No tenant is named. Nothing published describes the electrical topology, the cooling method, or on-site generation, so the campus's fitness for dense AI training cannot be judged from these facts. A 6 MW figure is a power input, and power is the binding constraint on AI scaling, but a number that small relative to training campuses means this site is more plausibly built for conventional enterprise load than for large training clusters.

New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, and only five publish any capacity figure at all. Those five total 111.3 MW, of which this campus is 6 MW, about five percent, ranking it fourth of the five. That 111.3 MW is a floor on the state's data center load, not a measure of it, because the other 43 facilities publish nothing. The data also does not cover utilization, contracted versus available capacity, or any announced expansion.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
